## R52 - TWO GATES CLOSED STATICALLY. `os_variant` is PID-1-only; the memory-exception path delegates to a cached dylib. 2026-11-27 01:55 PST

Offline, no pod. Sources: `kc.macho` (kernelcache), `libsystem_darwin.dylib` and
the image list from `dyld_shared_cache_arm64` (993 images), `ReportCrash`
(152,816 B) and the 16,802-path OTA list - all from
`homepod/oldfw/17M61/ota/root`. Shared-cache reads used the parser the author supplied.

### R52.0 *** HARD NEGATIVE: `os_variant_has_internal_content()` is not flippable. Three routes close. *** [V]

R39.8 left this "INFERRED to be kernel-pinned... unresolved - worth an hour".
It is now resolved, and the hour says no.

**Where the value comes from.** `_os_variant_has_internal_content`
(`0x18029481c`, libsystem_darwin) reads a cached word at `0x1ad6ff680`; if it is
`-1` it runs a once-initialiser at `0x180294d2c`, which is:
```
0x180294d44  add  x0, x0, #0x33c   ; "kern.osvariant_status"
0x180294d4c  add  x1, sp, #8       ; oldp
0x180294d50  mov  x2, sp           ; oldlen = 8
0x180294d5c  bl   sysctlbyname
0x180294d60  cbz  w0, <parse the bits>      ; success
0x180294d64  bl   0xfffffff...294f58        ; failure fallback
```
So the primary source is the kernel, confirming R39.8's guess.

**The sysctl is RW, and that is a trap.** The OID at `0xfffffff008662d68` has
`oid_kind = 0xc4c00004` = `CTLTYPE_QUAD | CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_WR |
CTLFLAG_LOCKED | CTLFLAG_KERN | CTLFLAG_MASKED`, no `CTLFLAG_ANYBODY`, handler
`0xfffffff007a4e36c`. "Writable" looks promising until you read the handler:
```
0xfffffff007a4e36c  ldr  x8,[x3,#0x30]   ; req->newptr - is this a write?
0xfffffff007a4e370  cbz  x8, <plain read>
0xfffffff007a4e374  ldr  x8,[x3]         ; req->p
0xfffffff007a4e378  ldr  w8,[x8,#0x68]   ; the writer's pid
0xfffffff007a4e37c  adrp x9, 0xfffffff0087d4000
0xfffffff007a4e380  ldr  x9,[x9,#0x188]  ; the current value
0xfffffff007a4e384  cmp  w8, #1          ; pid == 1 ?
0xfffffff007a4e388  ccmp x9, #0, #0, eq  ; ...AND current value == 0 ?
0xfffffff007a4e38c  b.eq <do the write>
0xfffffff007a4e390  mov  w0, #1 ; ret    ; EPERM
```
**A write is permitted only from PID 1, and only while the value is still zero.**
Root is not enough; `launchd` is the only process that may set it, once, early.
We have no code execution at all, let alone as PID 1, so this is closed.

**What closes with it** (all previously listed as open):
- **`/usr/local/bin/mount_internal`** (R42.6, R39.8) - the `os_variant_has_internal_content("com.apple.filesystems.apfs")` gate at `/sbin/mount` `0x100003a84` never passes, so the `stat` is never reached. This was attractive because `mount` is a launchd **grandchild** (no identity check) and runs every boot; it is nonetheless unreachable.
- **`/AppleInternal/Library/LaunchDaemons`** as launchd's second bootstrap path.
- **`PerformInLeanTestEnvironment`** boot tasks.

**Also resolved as a side effect: R39.3's `os_variant_is_darwinos()`.** It is
`0x180294b64` in the same family, fed by the same kernel word, so its value is
equally fixed on a retail part. R39.3's INFERRED conclusion - that the gate
"bites" on this unit because `SystemVersion.plist` says `Apple TVOS`, not
DarwinOS - stands, and the `rd=md0` second-byte hazard it describes is real.
Treat R39.3 as VERIFIED on the mechanism, INFERRED only on the bit's value.

### R52.1 *** THE R42 JETSAM CHAIN IS IN SERIOUS DOUBT: EXC_RESOURCE delegates to a dylib that EXISTS *** [V on existence, U on short-circuit]

This is R45.4 / the parallel reviewer's point 4, and the evidence now leans
against R42.

`ReportCrash` carries, as plain strings:
```
0x10001469a  "enableReportMemoryException"                  (a preference key)
0x1000168fb  "/usr/lib/libMemoryResourceException.dylib"
0x100016925  "ReportMemoryExceptionFromTask"
0x1000172b8  "EXC_RESOURCE: libMemoryResourceException not found"
0x1000172eb  "EXC_RESOURCE: ReportMemoryExceptionFromTask not found in libMemoryReso..."
```
So on an `EXC_RESOURCE` it checks a preference, `dlopen`s that dylib, `dlsym`s
`ReportMemoryExceptionFromTask`, and calls it - with explicit "not found" error
paths for both failures.

**The decisive fact: that dylib exists.** It is **not** a file on the System
volume (**0** of the 16,802 OTA paths; absent from the extracted root) but it
**is one of the 993 images inside `dyld_shared_cache_arm64`**. By the exact
mechanism R42.9 described - cached dylibs are not files on disk and dyld
resolves against the cache first - `dlopen` **succeeds**. The "not found"
branches are therefore dead on this build.

**Consequence.** A *memory* `EXC_RESOURCE` is handled by the memory-exception
machinery, not obviously by `-[CrashReport captureDiagInfo:]` -> `runDiagTool`
-> `popen`. That is consistent with two things already in the log: R42.4's
correction that neither binary importing `_system` runs as root, and the
existence of a separate **non-root** daemon `com.apple.ReportMemoryException`
(`UserName = _reportmemoryexception`, R45.4).

**NOT yet verified, and it is the whole question:** whether the delegation
*replaces* the diag-tool path or merely precedes it, and what
`enableReportMemoryException` defaults to. The unidentified third-ivar gate
`cbz w9` at `0x10001e42c` (R42.2) remains the likely switch. Until that control
flow is read, **do not spend a boot on the jetsam -> ReportCrash -> `popen` ->
`/bin/sh` chain** - R42's "THE BOOTSTRAP IS COMPLETE" headline is not safe to
rely on. (And per R48 its `/bin/sh` payload could not have been a shebang
anyway.)

### R52.2 Status of the offline queue after this session

| item | status |
|---|---|
| trust-cache / argv audit | **done**, R50 |
| asl.conf `>` takes an arbitrary path | **done**, R51.1 - verbatim, mode 0644 |
| does asl actually *write* the file | **open** - `_asl_file_open`, ~`0x100005f00` |
| Update volume rw at runtime | **open** - device tree has no `fs_mntops` for `update-vol`, i.e. no explicit `ro`, which is suggestive and not proof |
| `os_variant_has_internal_content` | **done, hard negative**, R52.0 |
| `os_variant_is_darwinos` | **done**, R52.0 |
| `ReportMemoryException` fork | **mostly done**, R52.1 - dylib exists, short-circuit unread |
| `_OSAGetDATaskingValue` (R42.2) | **open** - in the shared cache, now reachable |

### R52.3 Rules added

- **`CTLFLAG_WR` on a sysctl means nothing until you read the handler.**
  `kern.osvariant_status` is RW and still unwritable by us.
- **A dangling dylib path is not necessarily dangling.** Check the shared-cache
  image list (993 images) before concluding a `dlopen` fails - R42.9's mechanism
  cuts both ways, and here it makes a "not found" branch dead.
- **Do not rely on R42's bootstrap** until the `EXC_RESOURCE` control flow at
  `0x10001e42c` is read.

## R53 - RULE-INVENTORY PASS: the log already knew most of what tonight rediscovered. Three corrections to R45-R52. 2026-11-27 02:00 PST

A full-file rule extraction over all 11,672 pre-tonight lines produced a
complete inventory of standing rules (boot-killers, ramdisk environment,
physical/operational, volume hygiene, evidence/methodology, NVRAM). It is
distilled to one page at **`multipod/JOB-PREFLIGHT.md`**, to be read before
queueing any job. Three things it corrects in tonight's own entries:

### R53.1 *** CORRECTION: `strings` and `od` do not exist on the ramdisk - several of my readouts were silently empty *** [V]

R20 (L5693, L6033) lists the ramdisk's absent tools as `cmp, tr, strings,
readlink, basename, od, df, sort, uniq`, with R24.5 (L7600-7625) giving the full
present toolbox. I used `strings` and `od` in `whatami.sh`, `snapbuild.sh` and
`verdict8.sh`.

Consequences for tonight's results:
- **Jobs 618 and 620's "SystemVersion strings:" sections were empty because
  `strings` is absent, not because the plist failed to parse.** I had attributed
  it to the binary plist. The build identification in R47.0/R49.3 therefore
  rests entirely on the file-count/size/snapshot evidence - which is
  independently sufficient, so the conclusion stands, but the plist line was
  never read. Use `xxd`/`grep -a` on the raw bplist (R26.2 also records
  `plconvert -x` failing on every plist here with NSPropertyListReadCorruptError).
- The `od`-based non-zero-nibble figures in those scripts are meaningless. The
  disk4 verdict is unaffected: the `READ FAILED (size=0)` branch came from
  `wc -c`, which is present, and fired before `od` was reached. **disk4 remains
  unproven on this pod, which is the same conclusion.**

### R53.2 *** R45.2 WAS A REDISCOVERY, NOT A DISCOVERY *** [V]

R45.2 presented "the evidence channel has never been validated on the booted
OS; a ramdisk write proves only that the in-memory proxy changed" as a new
correction. **The rule was already in the log**, at L5466-5469:

> "Any NVRAM test must write through **iBoot** (`setenv` + `saveenv` over
> irecovery), not through `nvram` in the ramdisk. Reading a variable back in the
> same ramdisk session proves only that the in-memory IODTNVRAM proxy changed."

and the same confound is recorded at L5352-5364 as the thing that un-proved R5.
R39.7 then restated it for custom names. So the premise behind jobs 604-615 was
contradicted by a rule written two days earlier. R45.2's substance is right; its
framing as a new finding is wrong, and the real lesson is the one in R53.0 below.

### R53.3 *** TEMPERING R45.9: `boot-command` has a controlled HARDWARE negative; `recovery-boot-args` is the precise live channel *** [V]

R45.9 listed "boot-command / recovery-boot-args" together as the
highest-upside open item. The inventory separates them properly:

- **`boot-command` from NVRAM: hard negative from a controlled hardware test.**
  R13.1 (L6199-6222) set `upgrade-fallback-boot-command=fsboot` and
  `boot-command=upgrade`, both persisted in `/options`, and the cold boot's UART
  marker sequence was **identical line-for-line** to the clean-restore baseline.
  The earlier "retail NOR iBoot EXECUTES NVRAM BOOT-COMMANDS UNTETHERED"
  breakthrough rested on the **retracted** 949 file-hash marker. R41.8 re-opens
  it only as a static `[U]` question. **For test design R13.1 wins; R41.8 is not
  a licence to assume reachability.**
- **`recovery-boot-args` is the one real channel, and it is precisely bounded.**
  R41.5 (L11019-11069) enumerated all 29 iBoot env-getter call sites:
  `boot_args.CommandLine` (0x8300aad9c) has six writes, all in FUN_83000b8c4,
  and `env_get("recovery-boot-args")` is appended **only** if bit 22 of
  0x8300ab554 is set - set only by FUN_83000ffd0(1), called from 0x8300041c8 and
  0x830004410, both **recovery-mode entry paths**. So it reaches
  `kern.bootargs`, and only in recovery mode.
  Recovery is reachable without the physical trick: `auto-boot=false` + `reboot`
  gives a USB-controllable recovery prompt in ~6 s (L2992-2999), and
  `recovery-mode` is itself a boot task whose entire job is
  `nvram auto-boot=false` (R47.2).

That makes the recovery path the best-grounded untether lead on the iBoot side -
but it is a *boot-args* channel, so what it buys depends on a boot-arg-gated
kernel behaviour, and R41.5 killed the normal-boot boot-args family. Worth its
own design pass; not a licence to skip one.

### R53.0 The meta-finding, which is the useful one

Tonight's four instrument faults (PATH, `0x12AC`, the `only` guard, my `local`
scope bug) plus the NVRAM-proxy confound were all **either already recorded as
rules or directly implied by them**. The project does not have a knowledge
problem; it has a **working-memory** problem: 13,000 lines of log cannot be held
in mind while writing a script, and the rules are distributed across 50
sections, several of which retract each other.

Hence `multipod/JOB-PREFLIGHT.md`: one page, read before every job, carrying
only the operative version of each rule with its superseding history resolved.
**If a job is about to be queued and that file has not been read in this
session, that is the error.**

- **Dump the first 0x4000 of the `nand_syscfg` element.** The existing 128 KiB

## R54 - R6.1 ANSWERED, and job 535 was never actually run. The asl route is untested, not failed. 2026-11-27 02:10 PST

A full extraction of "raised then dropped, never refuted" items from the
pre-tonight log produced 79 such leads. Two of them matter immediately.

### R54.0 *** R6.1(a) ANSWERED: `WiFiPeerToPeer` is genuinely absent from BOTH disk and cache *** [V]

R6.1 (L5234-5252) is the item the log itself calls **"the single most valuable
unknown in the whole project right now"**: root `mDNSResponder` (20
entitlements) `dlopen`s `WiFiAwareD2DPlugin` every boot and fails only because a
dependent dylib is missing at a **System-volume path we can write**.

Question (a) - does it exist in any firmware we hold - is now answered for
17M61, offline:

| path | on the System volume (16,802-path OTA list) | in `dyld_shared_cache_arm64` (993 images) |
|---|---|---|
| `.../WiFiPeerToPeer.framework/WiFiPeerToPeer` | **absent (0 hits)** | **absent (0 matches)** |
| `.../DeviceToDeviceManager.framework/PlugIns/WiFiAwareD2DPlugin.bundle/WiFiAwareD2DPlugin` | **present, 129,776 B, mode 100755** | n/a |

So the plug-in bundle is a real file that loads, and the failure is at its
**dependency**, which exists nowhere on the device. **That path is genuinely
ours to create.**

This matters because of tonight's `libMemoryResourceException` result (R52.1):
there, a "dangling" dylib path turned out to be satisfied from the shared cache,
which killed the lead. **Here the cache check comes back empty, so the opposite
holds** - this is a true dangling dependency of a root daemon. R42.9's
"dangling dylib paths are a DEAD CATEGORY" was argued from (i) dyld resolving
against the cache first and (ii) AMFI's `mpo_file_check_mmap`. **Reason (i) does
not apply to this path.**

Question (b) - *does AMFI accept an Apple-signed dylib that is not in THIS
build's static trust cache?* - remains open, and tonight gives the place to look:
R48's verdict table has op 16 `file-map-executable` as
`conditional(root 1854)`, not a blanket deny, and R24.2 located AMFI's
`mpo_file_check_mmap` at `0xfffffff007c99c60` with its deny branch. The static
trust cache holds **578** entries (R21), so a dylib lifted from 18.3 or 26.0.1
would not be in it. Reading that conditional against a cross-build dylib's
cdhash is an offline job.

Question (c) - the cheap probe - is unchanged and still right: **plant a
deliberately invalid file at that path and see whether the `dlopen` error changes
from "not found" to a signature rejection.** One boot, no ambiguity, and it tells
us which wall we are at. It needs a log channel, so pair it with the syslog
collection.

### R54.1 *** JOB 535 PLANTED THE SYSLOGD/asl EXPERIMENT AND JOB 536 UNDID IT SEVEN MINUTES LATER, WITH NO COLD BOOT *** [V]

R50.2/R50.3 arrived independently at syslogd + `/etc/asl.conf` as the best
no-exec route. The log records job 535 as having set up exactly that, and its
result as "never reported". **The result was never reported because the test was
never run.**

From the runner's own records:
- **Job 535** (2026-11-25 18:40-18:42, rc=0): substituted syslogd's bytes
  (166,496 B) over `/usr/libexec/CrashHousekeeping`, planted
  `/etc/asl/zzpASLPROBE` (247 B), left `asl.conf` and the service cache
  untouched, then `snapswap.sh` deleted and recreated the sealed snapshot.
- **Job 536** (18:49-18:53, rc=0): first action after the mount was
  `subst-undo.sh` -> `-- CrashHousekeeping restored (55152 bytes)`, then moved on
  to the Wi-Fi firmware work.

Seven minutes, no cold boot, plant reverted. **So the asl.conf route is
UNTESTED, not refuted** - and it is now far better characterised than it was
then, because R51.1 establishes that an out-of-tree path is accepted verbatim
with mode 0644.

### R54.2 Why job 535's probe could not have worked anyway, and the fix

`route2/asl.probe.conf`, preserved on disk:
```
> /System/Library/zzpASLPROBE_RO/probe.log mode=0644 uid=0 gid=0
> /var/log/zzpASLPROBE/probe.log        mode=0644 uid=0 gid=0
? [= Sender zzpASLPROBESENDER] file /var/log/zzpASLPROBE/hit.log
```
**Both targets are unreadable from the ramdisk.** The System-volume path is
read-only at runtime (deliberately, as a fail-loudly signal) and `/var/log` is
the **encrypted Data volume**, which we must never mount (L4747). So even a
perfect run would have produced nothing we could read - the same
observability dead end R2.1b recorded.

**That is exactly the gap R50.4 fills:** retarget the `>` rule at a path under
`/private/var/MobileSoftwareUpdate`, which is the **Update volume `disk1s3`** per
the device-tree fstab - unencrypted, and mountable read-only from the ramdisk
with no hang (job 565).

**And the design can drop the risky half entirely.** Job 535 substituted syslogd
into `CrashHousekeeping` because it assumed syslogd would not otherwise run. Per
R50.2 **`/usr/sbin/syslogd` is already a root cached daemon on this build**, so
no substitution is needed: plant only the config file. That removes the binary
copy, the `.stock` backup, the restore step, and every cdhash/AMFI question from
the experiment. What remains is a text file on a volume we own.

### R54.3 Plumbing that already exists and should be reused, not rewritten

- `route2/subst-syslogd.sh` - correct PATH export, mount guard, `.stock` backup
  discipline, and the `/etc/asl/` plant. Keep the plant, drop the `cp` of syslogd.
- `route2/subst-undo.sh` - restores `CrashHousekeeping` and `racoon.conf` from
  `.stock`. Not needed if we do not substitute.
- `route2/asl.probe.conf` - the right shape; only the target paths need changing.
- **Do NOT reuse `route2/snapswap.sh`.** It deletes and recreates the sealed
  snapshot; R12 attributes the destruction of the live volume to exactly that
  pattern in job 560 (`panic: "Process 1 exec of /sbin/launchd failed, errno 2"`).
  Jobs 535-538 each ran it. With Apple's snapshot now deleted outright and the
  pod booting live, it is not needed at all.

### R54.4 Rules added

- **Before designing an experiment, grep the job history for it.** Job 535 built
  this exact test two days ago; it was reverted unexecuted and the log recorded
  the result as "never reported", which reads as a failure and is not one.
- **An experiment's observable must be readable from the ramdisk before the
  experiment is worth running.** Job 535's two targets were the read-only System
  volume and the unmountable Data volume.
- **Check the shared-cache image list before calling a dylib path dangling, and
  before calling it satisfied.** It cut one way for
  `libMemoryResourceException` (R52.1, lead killed) and the other way for
  `WiFiPeerToPeer` (R54.0, lead alive).

## R55 - THE SysCfg/NAND/DIAGS AREA ENTERS THIS LOG, plus a free observability channel and two real contradictions. 2026-11-27 02:20 PST

Source: a full read of `knowledge-transfer.md` (717 lines), `SYSCFG_WRITE_FINDINGS.md`,
`FINDINGS-2026-11-24-protopod.md`, the Nov-12 free-SysCfg-route doc, `TODO-POD.md`
and `sbprof/R47*` - documents this findings log had never incorporated. Done by a
delegated agent; the items I re-verified myself are marked **[self-verified]**.
Their own labels (`[verified]` / `[session]` / `[plan]` / `[inferred]`) are preserved.

### R55.0 *** A FREE OBSERVABILITY CHANNEL NOBODY HAS USED: NANDInfo over lockdown *** [verified on a real pod, per KT:410-417]

```
ideviceinfo -q com.apple.disk_usage -k NANDInfo
```
Answered by a pod in audioOS **with no exploit, no ramdisk and no jailbreak**.
Blob format: `u32 key, u32 count, count x u64`, little-endian. Keys:
**10 = boots, 11 = unclean boots**, 22/23 program/erase fails, 34 power-on
hours, 46 factory-bad, 47 grown-bad, **198 = SysCfg writes**.

**Why this matters for the current blocker.** Every channel in R45.8's table is
either denied, unreadable or unproven. This one is a lockdown query against a
booted pod - the same transport as the `info` action already in the runner, which
returned rc=0 at 01:07:44 tonight. It gives, for free:
- **a boot counter** (key 10) and an **unclean-boot counter** (key 11), which
  together detect *whether a boot happened at all* and *whether it was clean* -
  exactly what the obliteration loop and any panic-reboot would move, and
  precisely what we could not see without UART;
- a SysCfg-write counter (key 198) as a tamper check before/after any DIAGS work.
Reference figures on the bench pod (Nov 2026): 1,023 power-on hours, 361 boots of
which **118 unclean**, 13 factory-bad, 0 grown-bad, 32 SysCfg writes (KT:462-464).

**Add it to the runner as an action.** It is read-only and needs the pod booted.

### R55.1 Where SysCfg actually lives, and the write routes [KT, SWF]

- **SysCfg is NOT an effaceable locker.** The live pod's effaceable device is
  Capacity 960 / UnitSize 4096 / CopySize 1024 / CopiesPerUnit 4 - **960 usable
  bytes total**, so a 131,072-byte SysCfg cannot live there. The lockers hold
  keys and nonces (SWF:8-16, KT:620-623).
- It lives in one of the **ASP/ANS controller's own areas**, outside the user
  area and outside every `/dev/diskN`, with its own commands **0x37 read /
  0x47 write** [inferred] (SWF:18-22).
- Full ASP op list (KT:552-557): `0x00` identify, `0x10/0x11` user r/w, `0x13`
  flush, **`0x15` FORMAT_ALL, `0x16` FORMAT_USERAREA, `0x18` FORMAT_CLEAR**,
  `0x19` write-unlock, **`0x30-0x38` read / `0x40-0x48` write** over LLB, FW,
  UTILDM, DM, CTRLBITS, EFFACE, NVRAM, **SYSCFG**, PANICLOG in that order,
  `0x79` PPN fw version. Writes require `0x19` first.
- Area map (KT:472-486): LLB `asp0n2`, Firmware `asp0n3` (4 MiB), UTILDM
  `asp0n4`, DM `asp0n5`, CTRLBITS `asp0n6`, Effaceable `asp0n7`, **NVRAM
  `asp0n8`**, **SysCfg `asp0n9` (256 x 4 KiB, 128 KiB blob, `gfCS`)**, PanicLog
  `asp0n10` (1 MiB).
- **Inline AES-CBC in the ASP**: every I/O command carries an encryption flag;
  without the no-encryption flag the controller transforms data with a key Linux
  never sets (KT:458). Relevant to any raw-area read/write plan.
- **Write routes, safest first** (SWF:24-34): (1) **DIAGS `syscfg add` works
  today** for keys that fit on the command line; (2) from Nicotine/Linux, needs
  SYSCFG write support added to the driver, and the controller **only accepts a
  whole-area rewrite starting at sector 0**; (3) under XNU, find what issues
  `0x47` - **"the ReadOnly build analysed doesn't have it."**
- **PROVEN DEAD, do not re-walk:** the `AppleDiagnosticDataAccessReadOnly::setProperties`
  + base/stage/commit patch. Both `setProperties` (+0x160) and the low-level
  region write (+0x540) are **error-returning stubs**; STAGE/COMMIT call
  `arg1->vtable[0xb0]` expecting `containsRegion(OSSymbol*)` but OSDictionary's
  +0xb0 is `getCapacityIncrement()` - **type confusion**; and STAGE/COMMIT/flush
  have **zero internal callers**. The writable driver was compiled out.
  **"Do not flash the base+stage+commit patch."** (SWF:38-81).
- **NAND-swap identity re-provisioning works today** via `syscfg add` for `SrNm`,
  `MLB#`, `Mod#`, `Regn`, `WMac`, `BMac`, `EMac`. **Blocked:** `WCAL` (2,204 B)
  and `BCAL` (3,444 B) are too large for the DIAGS command line (KT:259-262).
- **Colour reconfiguration is [verified on hardware]**: `Mod#`, `CLCG` and
  `CLHS` must all agree, because the BLE proximity-pairing advert (service UUID
  `0xFE25`) is built locally from `CLCG`/`CLHS` (KT:136-152).
- **NEVER** (KT:382-385, 610-616): `FORMAT_ALL` (0x15) / `FORMAT_CLEAR` (0x18);
  write SysCfg, DM, UTILDM, CTRLBITS, LLB or Firmware; **run `NANDInfoTool`** -
  null-pointer panic in `TestNand.macho`, pod drops to DFU [verified].

### R55.2 Soft DFU is LLB DFU, and the PMU scratch is iBoot's NVRAM [verified from Apple's Astris scripts, KT:632-676]

- **hard DFU = SecureROM DFU; soft DFU = LLB DFU.** Astris uses hard DFU only on
  PMUs that hold a force-DFU GPIO through reset; the HomePod's **D2186 ("Adi") is
  not one**, so for B238/B238a Astris always falls back to soft DFU.
- Mechanism: halt the AP cores, write **`0xA0` to PMU scratch `+0x14` =
  `0x4014`** (IBOOT_ENTER_DFU), read back (up to 5 tries), reset the SoC so LLB
  sees the request.
- **PMU scratch is iBoot's NVRAM**: D2186 on **I2C0, address 0x74**, 16-bit
  addresses high byte first. `0x4000` debug, `0x4001` stage, `0x4002` error
  count, `0x4003` error stage, `0x400D/E` boot flags, `0x400F` state, `0x4014`
  enter-DFU. **Survives a SoC reset; lost when power is pulled.**
- **Hard limit: `gaster` cannot pwn LLB DFU** - checkm8 is a SecureROM bug. No
  Nicotine, DIAGS or SSH ramdisk from soft DFU. **Not an untether route**, but it
  is a second, software-only way into a DFU-ish state.

`TODO-POD.md:313-314` (R5.5) says "ProtoPod folder holds `dev_ibss.img4` /

The dev-ness is in the **loader build**, not the fuses: the ProtoPod iBSS/iBEC

## R56 - THE POD-SIDE SCRIPT LIBRARY, CATALOGUED. And the rule that silently voided three jobs' plants. 2026-11-27 02:35 PST

A full catalogue of `route2/` (**103 shell scripts**, 200,750 bytes) with every
job→script mapping, derived authoritatively from
`grep -H "pod-sh multipod/route2/" runner/out/*.log` rather than from comments.
Done by a delegated agent; items I re-verified myself are marked
**[self-verified]**.

### R56.0 *** THE BIG ONE: ending a ramdisk session without `umount` makes APFS DISCARD EVERY WRITE *** [V]

Job 598 (`persist.sh`) is the proof, and it is unambiguous:
```
| === 1: FREE TEST - did job 597's marker survive? ===
|   nf-live.txt from job 597: GONE -> writes from an un-unmounted session are DISCARDED.
| === 2: THE DECISIVE TEST - write, unmount CLEANLY, remount, look again ===
|   wrote nf-probe.txt (26 bytes) / sync done / umount rc=0 / remounted
|   nf-probe.txt after clean unmount+remount: PRESENT  <<< WRITES PERSIST.
```
The UART quoted in `redo.sh`: *"nx_mount:1619: reloading after unclean unmount,
checkpoint xid 1087, superblock xid 974 - **113 transactions discarded**."*

**Jobs 595, 596 and 597 all lost their plants to this.** `persist.sh` adds that
even the *insurance snapshot* was rolled past (snap_xid 896 > 892). So some of
what R38.1 read as a "decaying volume" and R34.2 read as plants vanishing was
**an unclean unmount throwing the transactions away**. This is a third mechanism
alongside the sparse-live-volume fact (R49.3) and `snaputil -r`.

**Rule: `sync; umount /mnt1` must be the last pod action of every job that
writes anything.** The proven helper, from `bootswap2.sh`:
```sh
remount(){ sync 2>/dev/null; umount /mnt1 2>/dev/null; sleep 3; mount_apfs /dev/disk1s1 /mnt1 2>&1; }
```

### R56.1 *** CORRECTION TO MY OWN `JOB-PREFLIGHT.md`: I listed `od` and `strings` as PRESENT. Both are ABSENT. *** [self-verified]

Job 589 (`hdik1.sh`) printed the ramdisk's complete own binary inventory —
`/bin` 21, `/sbin` 14, `/usr/bin` 68, `/usr/sbin` 12, `/usr/local/bin` 16 — and
**`runner/out/589.log` is the authoritative answer to "does tool X exist on the
ramdisk".** Cite it by name instead of re-deriving.

`od` and `strings` are in neither the inventory nor reality:
`527.log: od: command not found`, `518.log: strings: command not found`. `df` is
absent too (both `510.log` and `591.log`, in scripts that *did* export PATH).

**This is why R53.1's symptom appeared** and it is worse than I wrote there: my

589, 591 `ioreg -p IODeviceTree -n options`). The "pid 47 ioreg, Kernel data
abort" text appears in **no runner log** - it is from a UART capture. So the
honest claim is "ioreg has twice destroyed a hardware session", not "it panics in
every form". The operating rule is unchanged.

### R56.4 `nvram` writes need `-s`, and it is verified in the binary [V]

`plantsh.sh`, citing `/usr/sbin/nvram` at `0x100002794`: a plain set issues
`IONVRAM-SYNCNOW-PROPERTY`, which is **only a request**; the undocumented **`-s`
selects `IONVRAM-FORCESYNCNOW-PROPERTY`**. Every arming write should use
`nvram -s name=value`. Job 589 also captured the full usage, including that
**`-c` deletes every variable** and `-b` sets from a binary file.

This bears on R45.2/R53.2: a plain ramdisk `nvram` set may not even have reached
NOR, which is a *second* reason those readbacks proved less than they appeared to.

### R56.5 Code signing IS enforced on the restore kernel, and job 593's probe was void [V]

- `594.log` (`csprobe.sh`): a one-byte patch **inside `__TEXT`** at four offsets
  gave `exit=137` every time. AMFI and Sandbox are both loaded (`kextstat`).
- `593.log` reported `exit=0` for the same idea - because, as `csprobe.sh` says,
  *"job 593's test appended a byte to the END of a Mach-O, which lies PAST
  codeLimit and is therefore OUTSIDE the hashed region."* **That result proved
  nothing** and should not be cited.

### R56.6 Scripts to reuse, and three not to re-run

**Reuse:** `sysvol-mount2.sh` (the canonical tolerant mount, used by ~40 jobs) ·
`plantsh.sh` (the best-documented script in the library, ~60 lines of
verified-fact comments) · `blockdump.sh` (the model `dd`, with a writable-scratch
probe) · `nvprobe.sh` (its `try()` helper is the only form that distinguishes
set-failed / get-failed / value-mismatch) · `snapcmp.sh` (the decisive live-vs-
snapshot measurement) · `persist.sh` (found R56.0) · `hdik1.sh` (the tool
inventory).

**Do NOT re-run as-is:**

### R56.7 Landmine found and defused [self-verified]

`runner/617.job.ready` was still sitting in `runner/`, pointing at
`verdict8.sh` - **the one readback script with no `export PATH`**, which is why
job 617 lost its entire NVRAM section. Re-queuing it would have repeated that
failure exactly.

Both fixed: `verdict8.sh` now exports PATH as its second line and its `od`/
`strings` calls are replaced with `xxd`; the stale file is renamed
`617.job.ready.SUPERSEDED-2026-11-27`. **The runner queue is empty.**

### R56.8 Rules added

- **`sync; umount /mnt1` is the last pod action of any job that writes.**
  Without it APFS discards the whole session's transactions (R56.0).
- **`runner/out/589.log` is the authority on ramdisk tool availability.** Cite
  it; do not re-derive, and do not trust a tool's presence because a script
  calls it.
- **Never wrap a tool invocation in `2>/dev/null` when its absence would be
  indistinguishable from a negative result.** That is how `od` and `strings`
  failed silently in four of my own scripts.
- **No unbounded `find`, no multi-megabyte pipe into `hexdump`/`grep`.** Bound
  with `-maxdepth` and `| head`.
- **Use `nvram -s` for every arming write.**
- **Nothing fragile after the final `umount`**, and a `pod-get` of a possibly
  absent path goes last and guarded.

## R58 — THE 13.4.8 vs 27.2.1 FORK, DECIDED; AND JOB 621
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2)
================================================================================

### R58.0 — VERDICT: STAY ON 13.4.8. The reason is step 2, not sunk cost.

I had the shape of this project backwards earlier in the session and want it
recorded, because the corrected version changes what counts as progress.

I had been treating "userland code execution on the booted signed OS" as a
consolation prize — root on a signed boot, not an untether. That is WRONG, and
R41.1 is why: **this build has no APFS sealing.** The root filesystem's contents
are not measured, not signed, and not verified by iBoot. iBoot IMG4-verifies the
*kernelcache*; it does not verify the volume. Jobs 608–615 already proved the
consequence empirically — a system volume carrying our planted files boots fine.

So the untether chain is:

    1. Code execution on the booted signed OS        <- THE BLOCKER (0-for-38)
    2. Reach the kernel write primitive (UDIF/hdik)
    3. Kernel write -> loadable trust cache / AMFI defeat   (R24.4, R36)
    4. Steps 1-3 re-run every cold boot from OUR files on an unsealed volume

Step 4 is what makes it untethered, and step 4 is already ours. We do not need
a pre-auth boot-chain bug at all. That reframes the whole NVRAM/marker grind as
work on the one genuine blocker rather than as a side quest.

**And that is exactly why 27.2.1 is a dead end.** R35 established that both UDIF
defects (`decompressBufferRequested`, the `compressedLength` underflow) are fixed
from the 26.6 cycle. On 27.2.1, **step 2 does not exist.** A working step 1 on
27.2.1 would dead-end immediately, and we would have paid for it by discarding:
the decoded platform sandbox profile, the op table at `0xfffffff00755f268`, both
`mpo_vnode_check_exec` hooks, the launchd `__TEXT,__config` boot-task map, the
`kern.osvariant_status` handler, and every offset in R27–R56.

Decision: **restore to 17M61 and keep it off Wi-Fi.** 27.2.1 stays interesting as
a *disclosure* question (what exactly did they change, and when) — not as a target.
Note for later: the fact that a 13.4.8 pod OTA'd itself to 27.2.1 at all is itself
anomalous (the author has never seen it since ~OS 17) and the obliteration cycle in R46/
R48 is the obvious suspect for having triggered it. Worth one job eventually; not
on the critical path.

### R58.1 — RETRACTION: my iBoot HFS+ string search proves nothing. R20 stands.

Before writing the above I had drafted a different recommendation: stay on 13.4.8
but retarget from userland to **iBoot's HFS+ driver**, on the strength of R20's
correction to R19 ("iBoot HAS A SECOND FS DRIVER: HFS+"), which would be a
pre-auth parser reading flash on an unassisted boot.

I tried to verify the premise with a string sweep of `homepod/oldfw/17M61/iBoot.dec`
(692,800 B) and got: 0 hits for `HFS`, `hfs+`, `hfsplus`, `BTNode`, `catalog`,
`hfs_`; 10 hits for `H+`; and the filesystem-string sweep returned only
`%s:Decompressing DM version:%d` and `DM_Decompress`.

**This is inconclusive, not negative, and I nearly made R5.3's exact mistake.**
- R5.20: iBoot addresses strings with `ADR`, not `adrp`+`add`. An adrp-only
  reference scanner returns zero hits on strings that are certainly referenced,
  **so a null result from one means nothing.**
- R5.3 (hard rule): "absent is the easiest wrong answer in a cross-build diff";
  code must never be identified by byte or encoding pattern.
- iBoot is string-light by construction. An FS driver with no debug strings is
  the expected case, not evidence of absence.
- The 10 `H+` hits are, if anything, weakly *supportive*: `H+` is 0x482B, the
  HFS+ volume signature.

So R20 is neither confirmed nor refuted and **remains the authority**, having been
an instruction-level audit. If we ever want the HFS+ route, it needs an
instruction-level check starting from R20's own cited addresses — not a grep.
Filing this because it is the second time this session I have come close to
overturning an instruction-level finding with a weaker method (cf. R49.2 on
shebang argv, R49.1 on the obliteration loop). The pattern is mine to watch:
**a null from a weak method is not a finding.**

### R58.2 — JOB 621/622: settle R57.4 before anything else. Queued.

R57.4 is a genuine four-way contradiction on NVRAM persistence across a cold boot:
ramdisk-written `boot-args` was lost once and survived once; a custom name survived
three times and was lost once. **While that stands, every marker-based verdict is a
coin flip** — and step 1's verification is entirely marker-based. Nothing downstream
is interpretable until this is closed.

Leading hypothesis (R57.4): plain `nvram NAME=VAL` issues SYNCNOW, which is a
*request*; `nvram -s` issues FORCESYNCNOW (verified at `0x100002794`). If `-s` is
the discriminator, then **every pre-608 marker result written without it is VOID,
not negative** — which would retroactively reinterpret a large part of the null
streak.

Design, deliberately minimal:
- `multipod/route2/nvsync-arm.sh` (job 621) — two FRESH names so nothing existing
  is disturbed: `nf-plain` via plain `nvram`, `nf-sync` via `nvram -s`. Re-arms
  `root-live-fs=1` with `-s` per standing rule. Dumps `nvram -p` before and after.
- `multipod/route2/nvsync-read.sh` (job 622) — reads both back plus the

Properties that make this the right first job of the day:
- **No restore needed.** This is a property of the `nvram` tool, IODTNVRAM and NOR,

Preflight rules applied: `export PATH` (rule #1 — job 617 lost its entire NVRAM
section without it); no `tr`/`awk`/`od`/`strings`; no `ioreg`; no `disk1s2`; never
`nvram` under `/bin/sh -c`.

Queued as `runner/queue/621.job`, gated `only <ECID_POD3> <SERIAL_POD2>`,
`wait romdfu 3600`. 622 staged, not queued — it goes in after the cold boot.

## R59 — R57.4 IS CLOSED. IT WAS NEVER A CONTRADICTION.
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2)
================================================================================

### R59.0 — The discriminator is a FORCESYNCNOW before power-loss. 4-for-4. [V, pending 624]

R57.4 presented four rows and called them a genuine four-way contradiction. They
are not in conflict. **Nobody had tracked the sync flag per write.** Re-reading
every `nvram` write in `route2/` against R57.4's own table:

| R57.4 row | writing script | sync issued before power-loss? | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 538 -> 539 `boot-args=wlan.debug.enable=1` | `bootargs-test.sh` | **NO** | **LOST** |
| 604 -> 609 `nicsfix-test=preboot` | `nvprobe.sh:58` plain | **NO** | **LOST** |
| 593 -> 595/601/603/604 `boot-args=-v serial=3` | `bootargs2.sh:15` plain, **then `:16 nvram -s` bare** | **YES (bare global flush)** | **SURVIVED** |
| 608/611/614 -> ... `nicsfix-pre` | `plantsh:130`, `vehicle:89`, `vehicle2:78`, `jetfix:75` — all `nvram -s NAME=VAL` | **YES (per-write)** | **SURVIVED 3x** |

**Four rows, four agreements, zero exceptions.** The hidden variable was
`bootargs2.sh` line 16: a bare `nvram -s` with no `name=value`, which is a
standalone force-sync of the whole partition. It is the only reason the 593 row
looked like it broke the pattern.

Independent confirmation arrived free with job 622, which read NVRAM after an OTA
to 27.2.1 **and a full `idevicerestore` back to 13.4.8**:
- `nicsfix-pre=v614` — PRESENT. Written `-s` by `jetfix.sh:75`.
- `debug-uarts=3`   — PRESENT. Written `-s` by `jetfix.sh:73`.
- `bootdelay=0`     — PRESENT. Written `-s` by `jetfix.sh:74`.
- `root-live-fs`    — ABSENT. Also written `-s` (`jetfix.sh:76`), but firmware
  **consumes** it as a one-shot, so its absence is expected and is not a
  persistence failure.
- `boot-args`       — present with an EMPTY value: the restore reset it. (See
  R57.5: test the VALUE, never the name.)

Every `-s` write that firmware does not consume survived an OS upgrade and a full
restore. That is a much stronger persistence guarantee than this project had been
assuming, and it is a reusable asset in its own right — see R59.3.

### R59.1 — Mechanism: the author cold-boots by UNPLUGGING.

A plain `nvram NAME=VAL` sets `IONVRAM-SYNCNOW-PROPERTY`, which is a *request*.
The value lives in the in-memory IODTNVRAM proxy and reaches NOR when something
flushes it — an orderly shutdown will. **A power pull will not.** `nvram -s` sets
`IONVRAM-FORCESYNCNOW-PROPERTY` and commits immediately. Both property strings are
present in the ramdisk's `nvram` binary (57,296 B, arm64, pulled in job 623 to
`runner/files/nvram-ramdisk`).

This also explains why the in-session readback was always reassuring and always
worthless — the long-standing rule at L5466 ("reading it back in the same ramdisk
session proves only that the in-memory IODTNVRAM proxy changed") was describing
this exact mechanism without naming the cause.

### R59.2 — THE CORROLARY THAT MATTERS: the shebang markers were broken twice over.

Every planted shebang marker in the null streak was of the form

    #!/usr/sbin/nvram nicsfix-sh=ran

(`plantsh.sh:94-95`, `plant4.sh:70`, `bootswap.sh:79-80`, `bootswap2.sh:62-63`,
`vehicle.sh:55,66`, `vehicle2.sh:48-49`). **Plain `nvram`. No `-s`. And a shebang
line has no second command, so the payload cannot issue a follow-up sync.**

So even in the counterfactual where op 102 had permitted the exec, the marker
would have been lost at the unplug. The payloads failed for two fully independent
reasons:
1. R48: the compiled platform profile maps `process-exec-interpreter` (op 102) to
   an unconditional DENY, so the `#!` never execs at all. This remains the
   **sufficient** cause for the shebang route specifically.
2. R59: the marker channel those payloads used could not survive the observation
   method even if (1) were lifted.

**Status change: an absent plain-`nvram` marker read after an unplug is VOID, not
negative.** This does not resurrect the shebang route (R48 kills it on its own),
but it means those jobs cannot be cited as evidence about anything else either —
not about whether code ran, not about sandbox behaviour, not about volume state.

NEW HARD RULE: **a marker payload that cannot issue a FORCESYNCNOW is not a
marker.** Either the payload runs `nvram -s NAME=VAL`, or the evidence channel is
not NVRAM. Candidate non-NVRAM channels, in order: the `asl.conf` arbitrary-path
file write (R58.3 #2), the `nandinfo` boot counter (R58.3 #3), and the Update
volume (reviewer's suggestion).

Worth testing separately: because R49.2 established that XNU **does** split shebang
arguments in `exec_extract_strings` (`0xfffffff007a26de4`), the form
`#!/usr/sbin/nvram -s nicsfix-sh=ran` should pass `-s` and `nicsfix-sh=ran` as
separate argv entries. Whether `nvram` commits the pair before choking on the
appended script path depends on its argument-processing order — being checked
statically against `runner/files/nvram-ramdisk` now. Irrelevant on 13.4.8 (op 102),
but it is the correct form for any future non-shebang payload.

### R59.3 — Spin-off asset: a scratch channel that survives a full restore.

`nicsfix-pre=v614` crossed an OTA and an `idevicerestore` intact. Apple's restore
writes a known set of NVRAM variables and leaves unrecognised names alone. So a
custom `-s`-written NVRAM name is a **cross-restore persistent store**. Useful for
carrying state across the restores this project does constantly (build identity,
which experiment a pod is mid-way through, a boot counter of our own). Low
priority, but free.

### R59.4 — JOB 623/624: the controlled confirmation. Armed.

Retrospective 4-for-4 correlation across heterogeneous jobs is strong but is not a
controlled test, so it is being confirmed with everything else held constant.

**Design note, and it is load-bearing:** `-s` is a GLOBAL flush of the NVRAM
partition, not a per-variable one — anything pending at that moment is committed
with it. So a naive three-way (plain / per-write `-s` / plain-then-bare-`-s`) in
one session is **self-defeating**: the bare sync would commit the plain leg too and
the test would silently prove nothing. That is the same class of error as R57.4
itself. Hence a two-way, with order fixed:

1. `nvram -s root-live-fs=1`   (re-arm; rides the flush below)
2. `nvram -s nf-sync=A623`     LEG A — per-write FORCESYNCNOW
3. `nvram nf-plain=A623`       LEG B — plain, and **nothing** after it issues a sync

The bare-`-s` leg needs no controlled test; job 593 already supplies it.

Job 623 ran against the **live ramdisk** — no DFU cycle, no mounts, no volume
writes. Armed state confirmed in-session (both legs present in the proxy, which per
R59.1 proves only the proxy changed). `nvsync3-read.sh` (job 624) carries its
verdict matrix in the script so the interpretation is fixed before the result is
seen, including the "both absent -> check `nicsfix-pre` as the boot-shape control
first" branch.

Cold boot must be **by unplugging**. A clean reboot would flush both legs and void
the test; this is written into 623's own output.

### R59.5 — Housekeeping: job 621 failed and never ran; 622's matrix is void.

`621.log`: `sshrd` died at `act pwn` — `limit 45 gaster pwn` hit its alarm
(`Alarm clock: 14`, rc=1) and the runner correctly stopped at the failing step. The
pod had been sitting in boot-ROM DFU for 505 s before the runner caught it; `pwn`
succeeded first try in job 622 fourteen minutes later on a freshly-entered DFU.
**Provisional: gaster `pwn` can hang on a stale DFU session.** Not established —
n=1 each way. If it recurs, `act pwn` wants a retry-after-`gaster-reset`.

Consequence: 621's arm step never executed, so the cold boot taken after it was
spent for nothing, and **job 622's own verdict matrix does not apply** — it reported
"neither present" because the variables were never written, not because a boot
cleared them. 622's *incidental* `nvram -p` dump is what made R59.0 possible, so the
job was far from wasted, but its matrix is void and must not be cited.

Also logged against myself: I queued 622 while 621 had failed, and I staged 622
without queueing it in the first place, which is why the author sat waiting on a job that
was not in the queue. Both are mine.

## R60 — `nvram` FULLY DECODED. The marker channel has a one-token fix.
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2). Static, on `runner/files/nvram-ramdisk`
================================================================================

Binary: 57,296 B, Mach-O arm64 PIE, base `0x100000000`, `__text` `0x1000012b4`
size `0x1f00` (1,984 instructions — the whole thing is tractable). Pulled off the
live ramdisk in job 623. Everything below is instruction-level, not inferred from
strings.

### R60.0 — `NVRamSyncNow` at `0x100002140`, and the flag it reads

```
0x100002140  adrp x8, #0x100008000        ; __bss (size 0x13)
0x100002144  ldrb w8, [x8, #0x12]         ; gUseForceSync - the LAST byte of __bss
0x100002148  tbz  w8, #0, #0x10000215c    ; bit0 clear -> plain
0x10000214c  adr  x0, #0x100003b9e        ; 'IONVRAM-FORCESYNCNOW-PROPERTY'
0x10000215c  adr  x0, #0x100003b85        ; 'IONVRAM-SYNCNOW-PROPERTY'
   ... mov x1, x0 ; b #0x10000216c        ; SetOFVariable(name, name)
```
`0x10000216c` is `SetOFVariable`. Both branches pass the property string as *both*
key and value, which is Apple's `NVRamSyncNow()` verbatim.

### R60.1 — `-s` is jump-table index 17. Confirmed, not assumed.

The option dispatcher at `0x1000013a0` is a computed branch, not a `cmp` chain:
```
0x1000013c0  adr  x24, #0x100003548      ; u16 offset table, __TEXT,__const
0x1000013cc  sub  w8, w9, #0x62          ; index = optchar - 'b'
0x1000013d0  cmp  w8, #0x18              ; range 'b'..'z'
0x1000013d8  adr  x9, #0x1000013e8       ; branch base
0x1000013dc  ldrh w10, [x24, x8, lsl #1]
0x1000013e0  add  x9, x9, x10, lsl #2
0x1000013e4  br   x9
```
Decoded (entry × 4 + `0x1000013e8`):

| opt | handler | | opt | handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-b` | `0x1000013e8` | | `-r` | `0x100001658` |
| `-c` | `0x100001438` | | **`-s`** | **`0x10000168c`** |
| `-d` | `0x100001480` | | `-x` | `0x10000169c` |
| `-f` | `0x1000014ac` | | `-z` | `0x1000016b8` |
| `-p` | `0x1000015d4` | | `-h` | `0x100001f0c` |
| `-e -g -i -j -k -l -m -n -o -q -t -u -v -w -y` | `0x100001ed4` ("no such option as --") | | | |

`'s' - 'b' = 0x11` = 17, entry `0x00a9`, target `0x10000168c`:
```
0x10000168c  adrp x8, #0x100008000
0x100001690  mov  w9, #1
0x100001694  strb w9, [x8, #0x12]        ; gUseForceSync = 1
0x100001698  b    #0x100001998           ; next argv
```
**`-s` is undocumented** — it is absent from the usage text's option list
(`-x -X -p -f -d -r -c -b -z`), which is presumably why nobody on this project
treated it as load-bearing for years.

### R60.2 — TWO sync call sites, and they explain both surviving rows of R59.0

Only two `bl 0x100002140` exist.

**(a) `0x100001d70` — inside the argv loop, after every set:**
```
0x100001d68  bl #0x10000216c      ; SetOFVariable(name, value)
0x100001d70  bl #0x100002140      ; NVRamSyncNow  <- unconditional
...
0x100001db0  add x21, x21, #1
0x100001db4  cmp x21, x22
0x100001db8  b.lt #0x1000013a0    ; loop
```
So **every** `name=value` is synced the moment it is set — FORCESYNCNOW if
`gUseForceSync` is already 1 at that point, plain SYNCNOW otherwise. This is the
`nvram -s NAME=VAL` row (`nicsfix-pre`, survived 3× + OTA + full restore).

**(b) `0x100001de8` — after the loop, gated:**
```
0x100001dd8  adrp x8, #0x100008000
0x100001ddc  ldrb w8, [x8, #0x12]
0x100001de0  cmp  w8, #1
0x100001de4  b.ne #0x100001dec     ; skip unless -s was given
0x100001de8  bl   #0x100002140     ; standalone FORCESYNCNOW
```
With no `name=value` arguments the loop body sets nothing, but this gate still
fires. **That is precisely `bootargs2.sh:16`'s bare `nvram -s`.** R59.0's fourth
row is now mechanism rather than correlation, and R59 is closed on both legs.

Side consequence: `nvram NAME=VAL -s` (flag *after* the set) also persists — the
in-loop sync is plain, but gate (b) commits it afterwards. Order only matters for
`-d`/`-c`, per Apple's own usage line: **"Note that arguments and options are
executed in order."**

### R60.3 — THE FIX: `#!/usr/sbin/nvram -s NAME=ran` is a sound marker payload

R59.2 established that every planted shebang marker used plain `nvram` and that a
shebang line has no second command, so it could never sync. That is wrong — the
flag can ride in the shebang itself.

R49.2 established XNU **does** split shebang arguments in `exec_extract_strings`
(`0xfffffff007a26de4`), and appends the script path. So `#!/usr/sbin/nvram -s
nicsfix-sh=ran` yields argv:

    nvram  -s  nicsfix-sh=ran  /path/to/the/script

Processed in order (R60.2 + Apple's usage line):
1. `-s` → `gUseForceSync = 1`
2. `nicsfix-sh=ran` → `SetOFVariable` → **FORCESYNCNOW. Committed to NOR here.**
3. `/path/to/the/script` → no `=`, so it is a *get* → fails with "Error getting
   variable - '…'" and a nonzero exit.

**Step 3 fails only after step 2 has already reached NOR.** A failing get deletes
nothing. So the marker survives an unplug, and the nonzero exit is harmless for a
marker (it would matter only under launchd `RequireSuccess`).

This does **not** reopen the shebang route on 13.4.8 — R48's op-102 DENY kills the
exec itself and is independent. It matters because:
- it is the correct form for **any** future payload, shebang or not;
- 27.2.1's op-102 behaviour is unknown, so if that route is ever revisited the
  payload is already right;
- it retires R59.2's claim that the shebang form was *inherently* unsyncable.

Standing rule, amended from R59.2: **every NVRAM marker write must carry `-s`,
including inside a shebang.** Plain `nvram` in a payload is a silent data-loss bug.

### R60.4 — Method note against myself: two silent-failure bugs in one hour

My first two attempts to find xrefs to the sync strings both returned **zero
hits**, and I nearly filed that as "the strings are unreferenced". The cause was
my own parser: capstone renders immediates as `#0x100003000`, and `int('#0x…', 0)`
raises — inside a bare `except: pass`. Both sweeps were reporting parse failures
as absence.

This is the *third* instance of the same failure mode in this project, and the
pattern is now explicit enough to be a rule:
- R53.1/R56.1: `od`/`strings` absent from the ramdisk, wrapped in `2>/dev/null`,
  so missing tools read as empty output → phantom "blank paniclog".
- R58.1: adrp-only scanner on iBoot → false zero on HFS+ strings.
- R60.4: swallowed exceptions in my own xref scanner → false zero on both sync
  property strings, in a 1,984-instruction binary that references both.

**HARD RULE: a null result from a tool that can fail silently is not evidence of
absence.** Never wrap a probe in `2>/dev/null` or a bare `except`. Make the probe
prove it ran — count what it parsed (the corrected sweep reports "disassembled
1984 instructions" and "101 string refs" before any conclusion), and verify it
finds a known-present control. R5.3 said this about cross-build diffs; it applies
to my own tooling with equal force.

## R61 *** root-live-fs IS NOT A ONE-SHOT. THE NULL STREAK HAS AN UNEXCLUDED
##     THIRD CAUSE: THE POD WAS BOOTING THE SNAPSHOT. ***
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2). Device-verified, job 624.
================================================================================

### R61.0 — R59 CONFIRMED by controlled A/B (job 623 arm -> unplug -> job 624 read)

```
nf-sync   (nvram -s nf-sync=A623)  -> nf-sync	A623        SURVIVED
nf-plain  (nvram nf-plain=A623)    -> data was not found    LOST
nicsfix-pre (control, -s, yesterday, pre-restore) -> v614   SURVIVED
```
Same session, same boot, same unplug, differing only in the flag. **FORCESYNCNOW
before power-loss is the sole discriminator.** R57.4 is closed as an artifact;
R59/R60 stand on retrospective correlation (4-for-4), decoded mechanism, and now a
controlled experiment.

### R61.1 — THE UNEXPECTED RESULT: `root-live-fs=1` SURVIVED the cold boot

Job 624 also returned `root-live-fs	1`. The script predicted "expect GONE".

The notes claim the opposite, twice:
- L10128 (R37.9, job 601): "`nvram root-live-fs -> not found` <- **WE SET IT TO 1.
  The boot CONSUMED it.**"
- L10134: "**`root-live-fs` is confirmed read-and-cleared on boot.**"
- L10865 (standing rule): "`root-live-fs=1` **must be re-armed from the ramdisk
  immediately before every** [test boot]".

**All three are wrong, and R59 is why.** The writes behind them:

| script | line | write | job(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plant.sh`    | 74  | `nvram root-live-fs=1` — **no `-s`** | — |
| `plant2.sh`   | 73  | `nvram root-live-fs=1` — **no `-s`** | **599** |
| `plant3.sh`   | 102 | `nvram root-live-fs=1` — **no `-s`** | **601** |
| `plant4.sh`   | 104 | `nvram root-live-fs=1` — **no `-s`** | **602** |
| `verdict3.sh` | 75  | `nvram root-live-fs=1` — **no `-s`** | **603** |

Every one of them wrote it plain, and every one was followed by an unplug. So the
variable **never reached NOR**. It was not "read and cleared by the boot" — it was
never there at boot time to be read. Written with `-s` (job 623) it survives
untouched (job 624).

Corrected: **`root-live-fs` is an ordinary persistent NVRAM variable.** It is not
consumed, and it does not need re-arming. L10865's standing rule is retired.

### R61.2 — CONSEQUENCE: jobs 599-605 booted the SNAPSHOT, so the plants were not
###          in the booted filesystem at all

The boot-root resolution order is established (L6166, L7677, R29 at L8703):

    NVRAM root-live-fs != 0  ->  LIVE volume
    else                     ->  the boot SNAPSHOT

In jobs 599-605 `root-live-fs` was absent at boot time (R61.1). Therefore the
kernel took the **snapshot** path. The plants were written to the **live** volume.
**The planted files were never present in the filesystem that booted.** Nothing of
ours could have run, for reasons having nothing to do with sandboxing, AMFI,
trust caches, launchd, or markers.

This also resolves L10227's two readings, which were (i) `root-live-fs` doesn't
switch the boot root on this build, or (ii) it does but the damaged live volume
failed to mount and the kernel fell back. **Neither.** Reading **(iii)**:
`root-live-fs` was not set at boot time, so no switch was ever requested and the
live volume's health was irrelevant. L10231 ("any further conclusion about
`root-live-fs` drawn from jobs 599-603 is invalid") was right, for a reason it did
not identify.

### R61.3 — This cause covers the jobs that R48 does NOT

I retracted R46.0 in R49.1 on the grounds that R48's op-102 DENY was a sufficient
cause for every null. **That was too broad, and the retraction was partly wrong.**

Op 102 is `process-exec-interpreter` — it only bites a `#!` script. But jobs
599-602 planted **LaunchDaemon plists whose Program was `hdik`**, a real
Apple-signed binary. No shebang, no interpreter exec, **so op 102 never applies to
them.** R48 cannot explain those nulls. R61.2 can.

Current honest accounting of the streak:
- **shebang payloads** (`plantsh`, `bootswap`, `vehicle`, `plant4`'s sysstatuscheck):
  R48 op-102 DENY is sufficient and independent. Dead on 13.4.8. Also R59.2: the
  marker could not have persisted either.
- **LaunchDaemon-plist payloads** (599-602): **two live explanations, neither
  excluded** — (a) R61.2, the boot used the snapshot so the plist was not there;
  (b) the signed MRM cache is the authority and loose `/System/Library/LaunchDaemons`
  plists are not honoured. Job 625 confirms loose plists DO exist on disk, so (b)
  is about precedence, not presence. **These must be separated before the plist
  route is called closed.**

**The streak is 0-for-38 boots, but a large part of it was never a valid test.**

### R61.4 — Job 625: the OTA kill-switch targets, verified present

Read-only, ran in 624's ramdisk session. All three binaries exist where the signed
MRM cache says (`route2/mrm.orig.plist`, parsed offline — 183 LaunchDaemons, 9
OTA/asset-related):

| binary | size |
|---|---|
| `…/SoftwareUpdateController.framework/Support/sucontrollerd` | 353,408 |
| `…/MobileSoftwareUpdate.framework/Support/softwareupdated`   | 223,632 |
| `/usr/libexec/mobileassetd`                                   | 554,368 |

All dated Jun 30 2020, `root:wheel 0755`. Secondary surface also present:
`OTATaskingAgent`, `OTACrashCopier`, `NRDUpdated`, `seputil`.

**None of the three carries `RequireRun`, `RequireSuccess` or `RebootOnExitCode`**
— those keys are absent from all 183 jobs' OTA entries. They are ordinary
LaunchDaemons, not boot tasks, so a missing Program fails to spawn and the boot
continues (L10395, L10430). Renaming them is benign and reversible.

The auto-updater specifically is `com.apple.sucontrollerd`, via xpc activity
`com.apple.sucontrollerd.auto-update` (Repeating, Delay 60, Maintenance).
`mobileassetd` carries `com.apple.mobileassetd.metadata-update` (Repeating,
Delay 60) — that is how the pod *learns* an update exists.

Snapshot state: exactly one, `com.apple.os.update-AB5CC358CB3D0D177607B8CE65A71A156A475762`.
**No safety snapshot of ours exists** — take one before any volume write.

**And R61.1 changes the plan here too:** because `root-live-fs=1` persists when
written with `-s`, we do **NOT** need to delete the boot snapshot to make live-volume
edits take effect. Arm it once with `-s` and the pod boots live from then on. That
retires L11125's option-2 trade-off (destructive, loses the known-good fallback) for
this purpose.

### R61.5 — Method, fourth instance in one session

`otacheck.sh`'s loose-plist probe was `ls -l … 2>/dev/null | sed … || echo "(absent)"`.
The `||` tests **sed's** exit status, which is 0 whether or not `ls` found anything,
so the "(absent)" branch **can never fire**. The files happen to be real (the output
carries full paths), so the conclusion survives — but the probe could not have told
us otherwise. Same class as R60.4, R58.1, R53.1/R56.1. The rule stands and I keep
breaking it: **in a pipeline, check the exit status of the command that can fail, or
test the artifact (`[ -f ]`) rather than a pipeline's status.**

## R62 — THE LIVE VOLUME IS REVERTED BY THE BOOT. Plus five tooling corrections.
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2)
================================================================================

### R62.0 — The fact, cleanly established [V]

Job 626 planted 4 files on the LIVE System volume (2 LaunchDaemon plists,
`nf.dmg`, `nf-armed.txt`), verified all of them across an unmount/remount cycle,
and unmounted cleanly (rc=0). the author cold-booted — **confirmed by him directly, he
booted it normally before 627**. Job 627 found **all four GONE**, with the volume
otherwise complete (132 `/usr/libexec` entries, `launchd`/`hdik`/`nvram` present,
same snapshot `com.apple.os.update-AB5CC358…`).

Both competing explanations are excluded:
- **Not a snapshot boot.** Booting a snapshot leaves the live volume untouched; it
  does not delete files from it.
- **Not job 606's sparse-live hypothesis.** That predicted a gutted live volume
  (job 605 saw 49 `/usr/libexec` entries, no `launchd`). Here live measured **132
  entries with `launchd` present both before and after**.

Files vanishing while the volume stays complete is a **revert**. Job 600 observed
the identical pattern. So: **the live System volume is reverted on boot**, and
this has been silently eating every plant this project has made.

Critically, `plant3.sh`'s revert probe (write → umount → remount → look) **cannot
detect it**: it tests one ramdisk session, and the BOOT kernel is what performs
the revert. It reported "the revert flag is NOT armed. Planting is viable." in job
626, minutes before the revert happened. That diagnostic is retired.

### R62.1 — Mechanism NOT yet identified. Four jobs spent, honestly inconclusive.

R41.4 names the obvious suspect: `handle_revert_to_snapshot` writes
`apfs_revert_to_xid`/`apfs_revert_to_sblock_oid` at volume-superblock +0xa0/+0xa8,
and `apfs_root_to_xid` at +0x3C8 is "NOT consumed or cleared at mount … survives
an NVRAM wipe". **I failed to read those fields.** What was established:

- Container is `/dev/disk0s1`, NXSB valid (`4e585342` at +0x20). `/dev/disk1` also
  presents a valid NXSB.
- Offline parse of a 1 MB stage (job 633): `block_size` 4096, `block_count`
  0x3b9abf (~16 GB), `xp_desc_base` 1 / 104 blocks, newest checkpoint **xid 319**
  with valid fletcher64, `omap_oid` **0x3aa02c = block 3842092**, `fs_oids` =
  **0x402, 0x8dc, 0x8de** (three volumes). 53 checkpoint NXSB copies in blocks
  0–104, all checksum-valid, every `omap_oid` in 0x3a9ad7..0x3aa07c.
- **All container metadata is at the HIGH end of the disk**, which is why job 630's
  16 MB scan from block 0 found nothing.
- Job 634 scanned blocks 3837952..3846144 for `APSB` — the hits were **spurious**.
  Their `+0x20` magic read `06000000`/`02000000`/`00000000`, never `41505342`, and
  their byte offsets mod 4096 were 1273, 3106, … never 32. Unaligned matches inside
  b-tree data. **A raw `grep` cannot check block alignment or fletcher64, so it was
  the wrong tool from the start.**

**The correct method, for whoever does it next:** resolve `fs_oids` 0x402/0x8dc/0x8de
through the container omap b-tree rooted at block 3842092, offline, verifying
fletcher64 on every block. Do NOT grep for magic.

### R62.2 — TOOLING CORRECTIONS. The ramdisk has NO writable scratch. [V, job 632]

```
root_device on / (hfs, local, read-only)
devfs on /dev (devfs, local, nosuid, nobrowse)
```
`/tmp` **does not exist**. `/`, `/var`, `/var/tmp`, `/private`, `/private/var/tmp`,
`/mnt1`, `/mnt2` all exist-but-read-only. `/var/run`, `/dev/shm` do not exist.
A 4 MB write fails everywhere. **Scratch requires `/dev/disk1s1` mounted rw at
/mnt1 first** — which is precisely why `blockdump.sh`'s candidate list is all
`/mnt1/...` paths and `blocks-job.txt` runs `sysvol-mount2.sh` before it.

**What this retroactively voids** — every one of these wrote to `/tmp`:
- **Job 627's disk4 paniclog read.** I reported "read genuinely failed → the
  paniclog channel is unavailable." **That conclusion was wrong**; the scratch
  directory did not exist.
- **`plant3.sh` / `plant5.sh` Q2** (`dd ... of=/tmp/p.bin 2>/dev/null`, then nine
  greps). Every `panic 0 / Backtrace 0 / UDIF 0 / hdik 0` line those jobs ever
  printed was a grep against a file that could not exist. That is most of the null
  streak's panic evidence.
- **R57.3's "8 reads, 8 empties"** needs re-auditing per job; at least one (the
  1,048,576-byte all-zero pull in job 579) did produce a file, so the history is
  mixed, not uniformly void.

**UPDATE, job 635 (same session):** with the scratch bug fixed and
`/mnt1/private/var/tmp` confirmed writable, `dd` DID run and both `/dev/rdisk4`
and `/dev/disk4` returned **size=0**. So the disk4 paniclog read genuinely fails
from this ramdisk. That is now a real measurement rather than a missing-directory
artifact. The channel is **unavailable**, not merely unproven — but note this says
nothing about whether a panic occurred, only that we cannot read it here.

### R62.3 — Process: `wait audioos` must gate every boot test

I could not tell from my side whether the pod had booted between 626 and 627 and
had to ask. The `usb-events.log` poller only samples when a job polls, so it has no
record of a boot. But `mode_of` already maps a booted OS to `audioos` (0x12B0 with
a 40-hex UDID serial, or 0x12AC), and `wait` accepts any mode.

**NEW STANDING RULE: every job whose premise is "the pod booted" must begin
`wait audioos <secs>` before `wait romdfu`.** The runner then PROVES the boot
happened instead of it being an assumption. This hole has existed for the whole
project.

### R62.4 — Five self-inflicted silent failures in one session. The rule, restated.

1. R53.1/R56.1 — `od`/`strings` absent, wrapped in `2>/dev/null` → phantom "blank paniclog".
2. R58.1 — adrp-only scanner on iBoot → false zero on HFS+ strings.
3. R60.4 — bare `except` in my xref scanner → both sync strings reported unreferenced.
4. `otacheck.sh` — `ls … | sed … || echo "(absent)"` tests **sed's** status, so the
   absent branch can never fire.
5. R62.2 — `/tmp` writes on a read-only ramdisk, hidden by `2>/dev/null`.

Plus two non-silent errors: job 628 queued with `wait romdfu` while the pod sat in
a live ramdisk (stuck 9 minutes until aborted via the `abort` file), and job 629
comparing against `4e584253` — the hex for "NXBS", not "NXSB". The 629 script was
right to refuse rather than guess; that is the one thing that worked as intended.

**HARD RULE, now stated as a checklist item:** a probe must (a) never hide stderr
on the command that can fail, (b) check the exit status of the command that can
fail — not a pipeline's last element, (c) assert on the artifact (`[ -f ]`,
`-eq 4096`) before reporting any count, and (d) include a known-present control.
A null from a probe lacking these is not evidence.

## R63 *** SOLVED: WHY NOTHING OF OURS HAS EVER RUN. TWO CAUSES, BOTH NAMED. ***
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2). From the booted pod's own os_log archive.
================================================================================

### R63.0 — CAUSE 1: the boot mounts the SNAPSHOT. `root-live-fs=1` is IGNORED. [V]

From `runner/files/boot642-fs.txt` (rendered from `boot642.logarchive`, pulled over
lockdownd from the booted pod):

```
apfs_vfsop_mountroot:1502: apfs: mountroot called!
handle_snapshot_mount:490: mounting snapshot w/snap_xid 27 and sblock oid 0x3aa034
nx_volume_group_update:6358: Volume com.apple.os.update-AB5CC358...  is not in a volume group
apfs_vfsop_mount:1489: mounted volume: System
```

**Every** root mount in the archive — across several boots — is
`handle_snapshot_mount` with snap_xid 27. There is not one live root mount, and
`root-live-fs` appears ONLY in the `dsc/` string catalogue, never in emitted log
data. `root-live-fs=1` was genuinely committed to NOR (`-s`, verified present in
jobs 624/636/640/642) and the kernel ignored it.

**This settles L10227's two readings as (i): `root-live-fs` does not switch the
boot root on this build.** Not (ii), not R61.2's "it was never set" — it WAS set,
with `-s`, and had no effect.

Consequence: **the live volume is not the booted filesystem.** Every plant this
project has made was written somewhere the booted OS never looks. That alone
accounts for the null streak, before any question of sandbox, AMFI, launchd or
markers.

### R63.1 — CAUSE 2: `CleanupPreparePathService` reverts the live volume EVERY boot [V]

```
handle_revert_to_snapshot:4208: On next mount, volume will revert to snapshot
    'com.apple.os.update-AB5CC358...' w/snap xid 27
CleanupPreparePathService[91]: reverting system volume to snapshot ... succeeded. remounting...
apfs_vfsop_unmount:1681: /dev/disk0s1: unmounting volume 'System'
revert_to_snapshot:1156: Reverting to snapshot w/xid 27 and old sblock oid 3842100.
revert_extents_to_snapshot:1025: free'ing extents in main extentref tree 3842103
obj_cache_remove_reverted_fs_objects:1471: removing reverted fs objects for fs 1026: 28 - 57
revert_to_snapshot:1202: DONE reverting to snapshot w/xid 27
CleanupPreparePathService: mounting system volume read/write at
    /private/var/MobileSoftwareUpdate/mnt1 succeeded.
CleanupPreparePathService: Skipping snapshot com.apple.os.update-AB5CC358...
```

The agent is **`com.apple.MobileSoftwareUpdate.CleanupPreparePathService`**, a
userspace on-demand XPC service spawned under `softwareupdated`. It fires on
**every** boot and more than once per boot (16:00:08, 16:00:11 x3, 16:04:03 in one
archive). This is exactly the `handle_revert_to_snapshot` / +0xa0/+0xa8 mechanism
R41.4 named — driven from userspace, not the kernel mount path.

Located (job 644), and it is the ONLY XPCService in that framework:
```
/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/MobileSoftwareUpdate.framework/XPCServices/
  com.apple.MobileSoftwareUpdate.CleanupPreparePathService.xpc/
    com.apple.MobileSoftwareUpdate.CleanupPreparePathService
```
`softwareupdated` itself greps 0 for `revert_to_snapshot` and `fs_snapshot`, so the
service - not its parent - does the work. **One rename disables it.**

### R63.2 — RETRACTION: my job-638 omap result was a FALSE NEGATIVE

R62.1/R62 reported `apfs_revert_to_xid = 0`, `apfs_revert_to_sblock_oid = 0`,
`apfs_root_to_xid = 0` on System, Data and Update, verified by fletcher64, and I
concluded **"R41.4's mechanism is NOT the cause."** That conclusion was wrong.

The field is **armed and consumed within the same boot**: the service sets it,
immediately unmounts, the revert executes on the next mount seconds later, and the
field is cleared. By the time a ramdisk session reads the superblock - minutes and
a reset later - it is always zero. **The measurement was correct; the inference was
not.** R41.4 was right all along.

Rule this adds: **a field that is armed and consumed inside one boot cannot be
tested by reading it from the ramdisk afterwards.** Reading state after the fact
only sees the post-consumption value. The observation has to come from inside the
boot - which here meant the os_log archive.

### R63.3 — Also corrected: the paniclog and durability results stand, but re-read

- Job 640 (reset into DFU, plants PRESENT) remains valid and still proves the
  ramdisk's APFS writes ARE durable. That control is unaffected.
- R62.2's `/tmp` correction stands; the disk4 read failing with valid scratch
  (job 635) stands.
- R62.3's `wait audioos` rule proved its worth immediately: job 642 recorded
  `audioos after 42s`, so the boot was a fact, not an assumption.

### R63.4 — THE PATH, now unambiguous

Because the booted filesystem is the snapshot, **anything we want executed must be
IN the snapshot.** Live-volume edits are inert by construction. So:

1. Rename `…CleanupPreparePathService.xpc/com.apple.MobileSoftwareUpdate.CleanupPreparePathService`
   on live -> the revert agent cannot spawn.
2. Rename `sucontrollerd` and `mobileassetd` on live -> OTA neutered (R61.4: none of
   these carries `RequireRun`/`RequireSuccess`/`RebootOnExitCode`, so a failed spawn
   is benign).
3. Plant the payload on live.
4. **Delete `com.apple.os.update-AB5CC358...` and recreate a snapshot of the SAME
   NAME from the now-modified live volume** (`route2/snapswap.sh`, whose hardcoded
   NAME must be updated from the stale `E6E4715D...` to the live one).
5. Boot: the kernel mounts snap_xid of *our* snapshot, which now contains the
   payload and the renames.

Failure mode is mild, per R41.3: *"A failed name lookup FALLS BACK TO THE LIVE
VOLUME in both stages"* (kernel `0xfffffff0084c3d48` -> `0xfffffff0084c3d80` leaves
`w25 == 0`; `0xfffffff0084c364c cbz w25` is the live-mount branch). So a botched
snapshot name boots live - which is the other thing we want anyway. A botched
snapshot *content* costs a restore, which is routine here.

Job 644 confirmed snapshot and live are currently byte-comparable in shape (both
132 `/usr/libexec` entries, both 185 LaunchDaemons) and that the snapshot mounts
read-only cleanly - so the swap starts from a known-good base.

## R64 *** launchd PANICS ON A MISSING EXECUTABLE - AND THAT IS A PRIMITIVE ***
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2). From the pod's own paniclog.
================================================================================

### R64.0 — THE REVERT IS DEFEATED [V]

Job 645 renamed `…CleanupPreparePathService.xpc/com.apple.MobileSoftwareUpdate.CleanupPreparePathService`
to `.nfoff`, planted two plists + `nf.dmg`, and replaced the snapshot with one taken
from the modified live volume under the SAME name. After the boot, job 647:

```
com.nicsfix.mark.plist   PRESENT
com.nicsfix.hdik.plist   PRESENT
nf.dmg                   PRESENT
nf-armed.txt             PRESENT
XPC original path        still gone
/usr/libexec entries     132
```

**First time in this project that a live-volume plant has survived a boot.**
R63.1's agent identification was correct and the fix works.

### R64.1 — But launchd panics the whole system, and Apple names the fix in the panic

`/dev/disk4` finally read (262,144 B; earlier 128 KB reads returned size=0 - use
`bs=1024 count=256`), 32 copies of:

```
panic(cpu 1 caller 0xfffffff01ae51ed4): "userspace panic: File Radar to:
  [ launchd | missing executable ]. Set boot-arg
  launchd_missing_exec_no_panic=1 to work around. Job:
  'com.apple.MobileSoftwareUpdate.CleanupPreparePathService'
  Executable: '/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/MobileSoftwareUpdate.framework/XPC…'"
Panicked task 0xfffffff000b94800: 832 pages, 5 threads: pid 1: launchd
Kernel version: Darwin 19.6.0 xnu-6153.143.1~3/RELEASE_ARM64_T7000
secure boot?: YES
```

**launchd (pid 1) panics the system when a registered job's executable is missing.**

**CORRECTION to my own reasoning in R61.4:** I cited L10395/L10430 - "missing
Program -> `posix_spawnp` fails -> `RequireRun` unset -> benign" - to argue that
renaming these binaries was safe. **That applies to BOOT TASKS, which are a
different mechanism with their own flags. It does not apply to ordinary launchd
jobs.** Deleting a job's executable is NOT benign; it is a guaranteed boot loop.
This invalidates the "benign" half of R61.4's OTA-rename plan as written.

The boot-arg workaround Apple suggests is **not available**: R41.5 enumerated all
29 iBoot env-getter call sites and NVRAM `boot-args` never reaches `kern.bootargs`
on this build; `recovery-boot-args` is recovery-mode only.

### R64.2 *** THE PRIMITIVE: launchd WILL exec a binary at a path we control ***

The panic is the loudest possible proof that, on a normal unassisted boot with no
host attached:
1. launchd reads its job list,
2. resolves each job's `Program` path **on the filesystem we now control**, and
3. tries to `exec` it as **root**.

So the step-1 question is no longer "can we get launchd to run something of ours."
It is only **"can we satisfy AMFI."** A binary we author is unsigned and will be
refused; a binary already in this build's trust cache execs from **any** path,
because AMFI keys on the cdhash, not the location. That is the project's proven
substitution technique (job 535 put `syslogd` at `CrashHousekeeping`'s path).

This promotes two things from speculation to the critical path:
- **R6.1(b)**: does AMFI accept an Apple-signed binary/dylib that is NOT in *this*
  build's trust cache? If yes, the substitution space widens enormously.
- **R3.2's hardcoded-config-path list**: a substituted signed binary is only useful
  if it reads a path we can write. R3.3 closed the argv route (none of the 16
  arg-passing jobs passes a file path, and the cache is integrity-enforced so we
  cannot add arguments), so a **hardcoded config path** is the lever.

### R64.3 — The fix applied, and the tool inventory it exposed

Job 649/650: instead of removing the executable, **substitute a signed one that
exits immediately**. Checked candidates on the System volume:

| candidate | present? |
|---|---|
| `/usr/bin/true`, `/usr/bin/false`, `/bin/echo`, `/usr/bin/basename`, `/usr/bin/uname`, `/usr/bin/env` | **all ABSENT** |
| `/usr/sbin/nvram` | present, 54,256 B |

So `nvram` went in at the XPC path (the real agent stays at `.nfoff`). With argv[0]
only it prints usage and `errx(1)` (R39.6) - it changes nothing. Snapshot recreated
under the same name; checkpoint verified an executable IS present at the XPC path
inside the snapshot, alongside our plants, with `/sbin/launchd` intact.

Note for future substitutions: **the System volume has essentially no standard Unix
tools.** `nvram` and `hdik` are the reliable ones.

### R64.4 — Still unknown: do loose LaunchDaemon plists work at all?

`nicsfix-mark` was absent in job 647, but the panic happened at launchd startup, so
launchd may never have reached our jobs. **R61.3(b) is still unresolved** - this
boot could not test it. Job 651 is the first boot that can.

## R65 — LOOSE LaunchDaemon PLISTS ARE DEAD. The cache is the authority. [V]
### 2026-11-27, session 3 (day 2). Job 651, first boot that could test it.
================================================================================

### R65.0 — The clean test, at last

Job 650 substituted `/usr/sbin/nvram` at the CleanupPreparePathService XPC
executable path (R64.3), re-snapshotted, and job 651 booted:

```
wait audioos -> audioos after 156s      (boot PROVEN, no crash loop)
com.nicsfix.mark.plist   PRESENT        (revert still defeated)
com.nicsfix.hdik.plist   PRESENT
nf.dmg                   PRESENT
nf-armed.txt             PRESENT
nicsfix-mark             ABSENT         <-- our job did NOT run
/dev/disk4               size=0         <-- no panic
```

Every confound is now excluded:
- the files **are** in the booted filesystem (they survived, and R63.0 shows the
  boot mounts the snapshot we built them into),
- launchd ran normally (no panic, pod booted and stayed up),
- the executables both plists reference (`/usr/sbin/nvram`, `/usr/sbin/hdik`)
  exist, so neither could trip R64.1's missing-executable panic,
- the marker uses `-s` (R60.3), so a successful run could not have been lost.

**Conclusion: launchd does NOT read loose `/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist`
on this build. The signed MRM cache (`mrm.plist` + `.sig`, loaded by
`launchd_cache_loader`) is the sole authority.** R61.3(b) is closed, affirmative.
This also retroactively confirms the user's own call on day 1 - he filed the
audit's "dropping a LaunchDaemon plist is enough" claim as *contradicted-by-device*
and refused to let it into the plan. He was right.

### R65.1 — `/dev/disk4` CALIBRATED. It was never broken.

| job | state | result |
|---|---|---|
| 647 | after the launchd panic | **262,144 B, `panic` x32** |
| 651 | clean boot, no panic | **size=0** |

So `size=0` means **"no panic log present"**, not "read failed", and the channel is
readable whenever there is something to read. Two things had hidden this:
`bs=1024 count=128` (too small - use **count=256**) and the `/tmp` scratch bug
(R62.2). **R57.3's "8 reads, 8 empties" is fully explained and the paniclog is a
WORKING evidence channel** - and unlike NVRAM it needs no cooperation from our
payload at all.
